{
  "research_question": "How does the stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) affect mouse navigation performance metrics including Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "The 'Combined' paradigm yielded the highest success rate (0.7798) and the fastest mean Time-to-Target (2.56s), outperforming all other conditions.",
    "The 'Bright Visual Only' condition showed the highest success rate among single-modality conditions (0.7845) and the fastest Time-to-Target (2.61s), surpassing the 'Combined' condition in speed but slightly lower in success.",
    "The 'Sham' condition performed significantly worse than all others, with a success rate of 0.2733 and the slowest Time-to-Target (4.68s).",
    "Path Efficiency was highest in 'Bright Visual Only' (0.5036) and 'Combined' (0.5022), while 'Sham' had the lowest efficiency (0.3084).",
    "Average Speed was highest in the 'Combined' condition (12.83) and 'Bright Visual Only' (12.68), whereas 'Sham' mice moved slowest (10.74).",
    "Angular Dispersion (AD) was highest in the 'Combined' condition (0.3994) and lowest in the 'Sham' condition (0.2360), suggesting different movement strategies or stability profiles."
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Success Rate: The difference between 'Sham' (0.2733) and 'Bright Visual Only' (0.7845) is the most pronounced gap, indicating a critical role of stimulation in task success.",
    "Time-to-Target: 'Sham' (4.68s) took nearly twice as long on average to reach the target compared to 'Combined' (2.56s) and 'Bright Visual Only' (2.61s).",
    "Path Efficiency: 'Sham' (0.3084) was significantly less efficient than 'Bright Visual Only' (0.5036) and 'Combined' (0.5022), indicating more erratic or indirect paths in the absence of stimulation.",
    "Average Speed: 'Sham' (10.74) moved significantly slower than 'Combined' (12.83) and 'Bright Visual Only' (12.68)."
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Stimulation appears to be essential for successful navigation, as the Sham group failed the task in over 70% of cases. Among effective conditions, 'Bright Visual Only' and 'Combined' produce the fastest and most efficient paths. Interestingly, while 'Combined' had the highest success rate, 'Bright Visual Only' was slightly faster and more path-efficient, suggesting that visual cues alone may drive efficient locomotion, whereas the combination might introduce complexity or different behavioral strategies (higher AD) that prioritize success over raw speed/efficiency.",
  "limitations": [
    "The analysis relies solely on summary statistics (mean, SD, n) provided in the artifacts; individual mouse trajectories and variance distributions are not available for deeper statistical testing.",
    "The 'Bright Visual Only' condition has a smaller sample size (n=3323) compared to 'Combined' (n=48846), which may affect the robustness of comparisons involving this group.",
    "Interpretation of AD (Angular Dispersion) is limited to the mean; without distributional data, it is unclear if higher AD in the 'Combined' group reflects increased variability or a consistent change in strategy.",
    "No interaction effects between specific mice and paradigms can be assessed due to the aggregated nature of the provided data."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct a one-way ANOVA followed by post-hoc pairwise comparisons (e.g., Tukey's HSD) for each of the five response variables to determine statistical significance of the observed mean differences, specifically testing the null hypothesis that all paradigms yield equal performance."
}
